ex.en: I can't stand this heat.
This plant handles the cold well.
Hang in there a little longer and it's the weekend.

ex.s: 우리 가족은 밥 먹기 전에 기도해요.
ex.en: Our family prays before eating.
I'll pray that the surgery goes well.
Grandma prays every morning.
I never imagined that.

ex.s: 이 집에 사는 걸 상상해 보세요.
ex.en: Imagine living in this house.
Kids imagine all kinds of things.

fix.note: Opposite: 전반 (first half). 초반 = early part.

ex.en: He's in his late twenties.
They scored in the second half of the soccer game.
They say it'll rain later this week.

fix.note: Somewhat formal; 사람을 쓰다 is casual.

ex.en: The store hired two part-timers.

ex.s: 회사에서 새 직원을 세 명 고용했어요.
ex.en: The company hired three new employees.
Should I hire a lawyer?

fix.note: 대답하다 = to answer (a person). 답 = answer (to a problem).

ex.en: Please answer my question.
I knocked on the door, but no one answered.
My kid won't answer when I call him.
He's a real gentleman.

ex.s: 그 사람이 신사답게 문을 열어 줬어요.
ex.en: He opened the door for me like a gentleman.
Ladies and gentlemen, welcome.
At least let me know.

ex.s: 공항에 최소한 두 시간 전에 가세요.
ex.en: Get to the airport at least two hours early.
You should at least show basic manners.
Sprinkle a little salt on the meat.
I put on perfume before going out.
Spray on bug repellent before you go camping.

notes: Fixed odd collocations (shoes 견디다, 이사 고용, 다음 달 후반, text 대답), 잘되다 spacing, one loose translation. Dropped 저장 as a duplicate of 저장하다 (ev-14).
